evidence: The Fear and Greed Index jumped sharply from 60 to 74 on July 20, solidifying a transition into Greed well above both the 7-day mean of 59.1 and the 30-day mean of 44.0. This sharp acceleration demonstrates strong positive sentiment momentum recovering from extreme fear levels recorded earlier in July. Although higher greed levels carry elevated risk of localized overextension and profit-taking, the short-term 24-hour momentum remains modestly tilted upward.
limitations: Fear and Greed Index readings update daily and reflect composite lagging indicators rather than real-time order flow.
Snapshot availability and later revisions are caller-attested, not independently verified.
